findings.rule: AC-002 fail-safe: a declared release step must not disappear silently (HTML comment handling diverges from rendering)
findings.evidence: unfenced() treats any '<!--' left on a line after removing same-line '<!--...-->' pairs as the start of a multi-line comment, wherever it sits, even inside inline code. CommonMark only opens an HTML comment block when the line starts with '<!--'; an unclosed '<!--' in the middle of a line, or inside a code span, renders as text. Probe: '## Implementation Plan / Keep the `<!--` marker style of the skills. / ### Step 1 — A / ### Step 2 — Sign / **Evidence class:** release' gives plan_steps() == [] and evidence_class_errors() == []. A temp project with that plan has no pending release item, and the ship progression passes without proof. No repo plan has such a line today (grep: 0), so this is rare. It is the same class of silent loss that rounds 0 and 1 rated as warnings.
findings.correction: Open a multi-line comment only when the line, after up to 3 spaces, starts with '<!--'. Remove same-line comments after inline code spans are stripped, or leave them. Alternatively fail closed: when a comment or fence is still open at the end of the document, evidence_class_errors reports it. Add the inline-code case to test_quoted_or_hidden_evidence_lines_are_ignored or to a fail-closed test.

findings.rule: Robustness against hostile input; the module docstring (line 6) claims every pattern is linear
findings.evidence: _COMMENT = r'<!--.*?-->' backtracks quadratically on a line with many unclosed '<!--': the lazy group scans to the end of the line from every opener. Measured with unfenced('<!--'*n): 0.28 s at n=5000 (20 KB line), 4.6 s at n=20000 (80 KB), 76.5 s at n=80000 (320 KB). unfenced runs on every plan validate, every spec-implement or spec-feature goal render, and every ship gate, and on implementation.md when a release step exists. This is far less severe than the round-1 _HEADING blow-up (49.7 s at 4 KB): it needs a crafted single line of 100 KB or more. The round-1 regex fix is closed: '# a'+20000 spaces+'x' and the other patterns stay at 0.0 s up to 80000 characters.
findings.correction: Remove same-line comments with a str.find loop: find '<!--', then find '-->' from that point, slice, and repeat. Or use a single pass that stops at the first unclosed opener. Extend test_long_whitespace_runs_stay_linear with a line of 20000 '<!--'.

findings.rule: AC-002 robustness: an announced proof must not satisfy /spec-ship (round-0/1 placeholder warning, partly closed again)
findings.evidence: The listed tokens are now rejected (17 parametrized cells, including '⏳ Pending notarization', '(pending)', '<receipt path>', '_pending_', 'x', '?'). The check is still a denylist of first words and marks. These cells are accepted as proof, and require_progression(..., 'ship') returns READY in a temp project: 'To be signed at release', 'Deferred to release', 'Still pending', '⌛ Pending' (U+231B, not U+23F3), 'Yet to be produced', 'In progress', '...'. 'Release build (pending)', 'Signed build: pending', 'Coming at release', '✅ pending' and '…' also pass is_proof(). Several of these are natural ways to write a deferred proof. execution-rules.md says a cell that only announces a proof is not one.
findings.correction: Invert the check and accept only a cell that names something checkable: a repo path or file name with an extension, a URL, or an identifier with a digit (build or receipt number). Otherwise reject any cell that contains a pending, deferred, 'to be', 'yet', 'in progress' or 'later' token anywhere, not only as the first word, and strip any leading emoji before matching. Add the cells above to test_announced_proof_keeps_release_pending.

findings.evidence: Every shape named in rounds 0 and 1 is now rejected and tested: whole bold, *...*, plain, double space, in a heading, #### heading, __...__ on a numbered item, table cell. These forms still neither bind nor report, so the step stays local: '**Evidence-class:** release', '**EvidenceClass:** release', '**Evidence:** release'. A line that closes a multi-line comment ('-->**Evidence class:** release') is dropped whole. '**Evidence class** release' (no colon) binds correctly.
findings.correction: Optional: let _ANY_CLASS accept '[ \t_-]*' between the two words, and keep the text after '-->' on a comment-closing line.

findings.evidence: In heading mode a step runs until the next Step heading or the end of the section. A sibling non-step heading does not close it. Probe: '### Step 1 — A / ### Rollout / **Evidence class:** release / ### Step 2 — B' makes Step 1 the release step. A heading such as '### Step-by-step notes' opens an unnumbered step with an ordinal label, and that label can collide ('Step 2 appears 2 times'). Both fail toward more proof or a clear error, never toward less proof. The numbered intro list collision from round 1 (info) is unchanged.
findings.correction: Optional: close the current step on a heading at the same or a shallower depth than the step heading. Require a digit or a separator after 'Step' for an unnumbered step heading.
